# Functional Requirements Specification (FRS) Template: Water Distribution SCADA Upgrade

**Template version:** 1.0
**Intended users:** Consulting engineers preparing utility-specific FRS documents

---

## How to Use This Template

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE**
> - Text in `[SQUARE BRACKETS]` is a placeholder. Replace it or delete it.
> - Blocks marked **AUTHOR GUIDANCE** are instructions for you. Delete them before issue.
> - Numeric values shown as `[default: X]` are typical starting points, not recommendations for any particular utility. Confirm every value with the utility's operations staff and record who confirmed it in the traceability matrix (Appendix E).
> - Write each requirement as one testable "shall" statement. Use "should" only for preferences, and "may" only for options. Don't mix them inside a requirement.
> - Describe **what** the system must do. Leave **how** to the integrator unless the utility has a standard, such as a mandated PLC platform. When you do constrain the how, record the reason in the Rationale field.
> - Delete sections that don't apply, but leave the heading in place with "Not applicable – [reason]". This keeps numbering consistent across projects and shows that the omission was deliberate.

### Requirement Format

Every requirement uses this structure:

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| **ID** | `[AREA]-[NNN]`, e.g. `BPS-010`. Never reuse or renumber IDs after first issue; mark withdrawn requirements as "Deleted". |
| **Requirement** | One "shall" statement |
| **Rationale** | Why the requirement exists |
| **Source** | Utility standard, regulation, workshop, or operator interview (with date) |
| **Priority** | M = Mandatory, D = Desirable, O = Optional |
| **Verification** | I = Inspection, A = Analysis, D = Demonstration, T = Test |
| **Acceptance criteria** | Observable pass/fail condition |

---

## 1. Introduction

### 1.1 Purpose
[State that this document defines the functional requirements for upgrading the [UTILITY] SCADA system. Name the intended readers: the utility, the system integrator, and the design engineers.]

### 1.2 Scope
**In scope:** [e.g., central SCADA servers, HMI, historian, telemetry network, PLCs at 6 booster pump stations (BPS) and 3 elevated reservoirs, control narratives, cybersecurity, migration, testing, training]

**Out of scope:** [e.g., treatment plant process control, AMI/metering, mechanical pump replacement, civil works]

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** Scope disputes are the most common cause of change orders, so list the exclusions explicitly. Also define each interface boundary precisely. For example: "Scope ends at the PLC terminal block for the existing MCC run-status contact."

### 1.3 Definitions and Abbreviations

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| BPS | Booster Pump Station |
| Call | A command or permissive for a pump to run, generated from a remote level |
| Duty / Standby | Pump designated to run first / pump available to replace the duty pump on failure |
| Lead / Lag | First pump to start / additional pump started on increased demand |
| Stale data | A value whose source has not been confirmed as updated within its defined timeout |
| Fail-safe state | The defined state a function adopts when its required inputs are lost or invalid |
| HMI | Human-Machine Interface |
| RTU / PLC | Remote Terminal Unit / Programmable Logic Controller |
| [add as needed] | |

### 1.4 Referenced Standards and Documents

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** List only what applies in this jurisdiction, and confirm current editions. Typical references:
> - ISA-18.2 / IEC 62682 – Alarm management
> - ISA-101 – HMI design
> - ISA/IEC 62443 series – Industrial cybersecurity
> - AWWA cybersecurity guidance and the use-case tool (US), or the national equivalent
> - Applicable water-sector regulations, e.g. risk and resilience assessment requirements, and drinking water regulator reporting rules
> - The national radio licensing authority's conditions for the utility's licensed radio channels
> - Utility standards: [tag naming, HMI style guide, PLC programming standard, IT security policy]

---

## 2. System Overview

### 2.1 Existing System
[Describe the current architecture, platforms, versions, known deficiencies, and operator pain points. Attach the existing architecture drawing.]

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** Interview operators as well as managers. Record pain points, such as nuisance alarms, slow polling, or pumps cycling, because these become requirements. List any undocumented logic you find in existing PLCs. Inter-site calls are often hidden there.

### 2.2 Proposed System Architecture

[Insert architecture diagram reference: Drawing [NO.]]

Typical configuration:
- Central SCADA: redundant (hot-standby) servers at [PRIMARY LOCATION], optional disaster-recovery node at [SECONDARY LOCATION]
- Historian: [integrated / separate], with [DMZ replica for business users]
- Telemetry: licensed radio (primary), cellular (backup) at each remote site
- One PLC at each remote site, with local operator interface [HMI panel / none]

### 2.3 Site Register

| Site ID | Name | Type | Key Equipment | Primary Comms | Backup Comms | Called From |

| BPS-01 | [NAME] | Booster | [2 × 75 kW, VFD] | Licensed radio | Cellular | RES-01 |
| BPS-02 | | Booster | | | | |
| BPS-03 | | Booster | | | | RES-02 |
| BPS-04 | | | | | | |
| BPS-05 | | | | | | |
| BPS-06 | | | | | | |

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** The "Called From" column is critical. Every inter-site dependency must appear here and must have a matching requirement in Section 5.8. If one reservoir calls several stations, or one station is called from several reservoirs, record each relationship separately.

---

## 3. Users and Roles

| Role | Typical Functions | Access Level |
|---|---|---|
| Operator | Monitor, acknowledge alarms, change modes, start/stop | Operate |
| Senior Operator / Supervisor | As operator, plus setpoint changes within limits | Supervise |
| Control/Instrument Technician | Calibration, tuning, PLC diagnostics | Engineer |
| SCADA Administrator | User accounts, configuration, backups | Admin |
| Management / Engineering | Read-only dashboards, reports | View |
| Vendor / Integrator (remote) | Supervised remote support | Time-limited, approved |

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** Confirm the role list against the utility's staffing. Small utilities often combine roles, but the access levels should stay separate. Record the hours when the control room is staffed, because unstaffed periods drive the requirements for alarm callout (Section 5.3).

---

## 4. Operating Philosophy

### 4.1 Control Hierarchy
Control authority, from highest to lowest:
1. **Local Hand** – at the motor starter or VFD. Bypasses the PLC except for hardwired safety interlocks.
2. **Local Auto / Local Manual** – at the site PLC operator interface.
3. **Remote Manual** – the SCADA operator commands the equipment.
4. **Remote Auto** – the site PLC executes automatic control using local and inter-site data.

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** State the fundamental principle explicitly: **automatic control resides in the site PLCs. The central SCADA supervises but does not perform closed-loop control.** Loss of the central servers must not stop the water supply. If the utility wants a different arrangement, document the reason and the failure consequences.

### 4.2 Mode Transfer
[Define how modes are selected (physical selector or HMI), which mode has priority, and the bumpless transfer behavior.]

### 4.3 Hardwired Safety Interlocks
List the interlocks that must operate independently of the PLC, such as low suction pressure, high discharge pressure, motor thermal protection, and emergency stop.

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** Any interlock that protects people or equipment from immediate damage should be hardwired. It should not depend on PLC logic or on communications.

### 4.4 Degraded Operation Philosophy
Define the utility's stated priorities when information is lost, for example:
1. Protect public health: maintain pressure and avoid backflow.
2. Protect assets: no dry-running, no reservoir overflow.
3. Minimize water loss.

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** Get this ranking signed off by the utility. It settles the hardest design choice in the system: what a booster does when it can't see its reservoir. Running risks overflow; stopping risks low pressure or loss of supply. The right answer depends on local hydraulics, overflow consequences, alternate supplies, and response times. Don't decide it yourself.

---

## 5. Functional Requirements

### 5.1 Central SCADA Servers and Redundancy

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** Define failover in measurable terms: switchover time, data loss tolerated, and whether operator sessions survive. Also require the integrator to *demonstrate* failover during FAT and SAT.

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| SRV-001 | The SCADA system shall operate with redundant servers in a primary/standby configuration such that failure of either server does not interrupt monitoring or control. | M | T |
| SRV-002 | Server failover shall complete automatically within `[default: 30 s]` without operator action. | M | T |
| SRV-003 | No historian data shall be lost during server failover; remote sites shall buffer data for at least `[default: 72 h]` and backfill on reconnection. | M | T |
| SRV-004 | The system shall alarm on loss of server redundancy. | M | T |
| SRV-005 | [Disaster recovery node requirements, if applicable] | | |

### 5.2 Human-Machine Interface (HMI)

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** Refer to the utility's style guide if one exists. If not, require an ISA-101-aligned design: muted backgrounds, color reserved for abnormal conditions, and a display hierarchy from overview to station to detail. Include data-quality indication. Operators must always be able to tell a live value from a stale one.

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| HMI-001 | The HMI shall provide a display hierarchy: system overview (Level 1), site overview (Level 2), equipment detail (Level 3), and diagnostics (Level 4). | M | I |
| HMI-002 | The system overview shall show, on one screen, the status of all BPS and reservoirs, all reservoir levels, and the comms status of every site. | M | D |
| HMI-003 | Any value that is stale, out of range, or manually substituted shall be visually distinguished from live values. | M | T |
| HMI-004 | Display call-up time shall not exceed `[default: 2 s]`. | M | T |
| HMI-005 | Operator setpoint entries shall be limited to engineer-configured ranges and shall require confirmation. | M | T |

### 5.3 Alarm Management

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** Require an alarm philosophy document as a deliverable (Section 10), aligned with ISA-18.2. Every alarm needs a defined operator response; an alarm without one should be an event instead. Define after-hours callout: method (SMS, voice, app), escalation chain, and acknowledgement timeout.

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| ALM-001 | Alarms shall be classified into at least `[default: 3]` priorities, defined in the alarm philosophy. | M | I |
| ALM-002 | The system shall support alarm shelving with mandatory reason and automatic expiry. | D | T |
| ALM-003 | Critical alarms shall initiate callout to on-call staff within `[default: 60 s]` when unacknowledged at the HMI, escalating after `[default: 15 min]`. | M | T |
| ALM-004 | The alarm system shall log all alarm state changes, acknowledgements, and shelving actions with user ID and timestamp. | M | T |
| ALM-005 | Comms failure at a site shall suppress that site's consequential alarms while raising a single site comms alarm. | D | T |

### 5.4 Historian and Reporting

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| HIS-001 | All analog process values shall be historized at `[default: 1 min]` resolution or by deadband, retained online for `[default: 5 years]`. | M | I/T |
| HIS-002 | Timestamps shall be applied at the source PLC where supported. | D | T |
| HIS-003 | The system shall produce [daily operations, pump runtime/starts, regulatory compliance] reports. | M | D |
| HIS-004 | Business users shall access historian data via a replica in the DMZ, not via the control network. | M | I |

### 5.5 Telemetry and Communications

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** Base these requirements on a radio path study; require one if none exists. State update times per data class instead of a single global poll rate. Decide whether inter-site calls travel peer-to-peer (reservoir PLC → BPS PLC) or through the central SCADA (reservoir → master → BPS). Peer-to-peer removes the central servers as a single point of failure for supply. Through-master is simpler to manage. Whichever path is chosen, document it in 5.8.

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| COM-001 | Each remote site shall communicate via licensed radio as the primary path and cellular as the backup path. | M | I |
| COM-002 | Failover from primary to backup shall be automatic and complete within `[default: 60 s]` of primary path loss detection. | M | T |
| COM-003 | The system shall return to the primary path automatically after it has been stable for `[default: 10 min]`. | M | T |
| COM-004 | Data required for inter-site control shall update at intervals not exceeding `[default: 15 s]` on primary and `[default: 30 s]` on backup. | M | T |
| COM-005 | Each communications path shall be monitored by a heartbeat; path status shall be displayed and alarmed. | M | T |
| COM-006 | Cellular communications shall use a private APN or encrypted tunnel; no site shall be reachable from the public internet. | M | I/T |
| COM-007 | Radio installation shall comply with the conditions of licence [LICENCE NO.]. | M | I |

### 5.6 Site PLCs

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLC-001 | Each site PLC shall execute its control functions independently of the central SCADA. | M | T |
| PLC-002 | Each PLC shall be powered by a UPS providing `[default: 4 h]` runtime, with UPS status monitored. | M | T |
| PLC-003 | PLC programs shall comply with [UTILITY PLC PROGRAMMING STANDARD]. | M | I |
| PLC-004 | Each PLC shall detect analog signal failure (e.g. `< 3.8 mA` or `> 20.5 mA`) and flag the value as bad quality. | M | T |
| PLC-005 | Setpoints and configuration shall be retained through power loss. | M | T |

### 5.7 Booster Pump Station Control (General)

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** Write a requirement set for each station, or a common set plus a per-station parameter table (preferred, see Appendix B). Cover duty/standby rotation, lead/lag, minimum run and off times, maximum starts per hour (from the motor manufacturer), suction and discharge protection, and VFD speed control where applicable.

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| BPS-001 | Duty pump assignment shall rotate `[default: on each start / daily / by runtime]`. | M | T |
| BPS-002 | On failure of the duty pump to start or run, the standby pump shall start automatically, and an alarm shall be raised. | M | T |
| BPS-003 | Pump starts shall be limited to `[per motor data: e.g. 6]` per hour per pump. | M | T |
| BPS-004 | Pumps shall be prevented from running when suction pressure is below `[SETPOINT]` (hardwired and PLC). | M | T |

### 5.8 Inter-Site Control (Reservoir-Called Boosters)

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** This is the highest-risk section. For each relationship in the Site Register, specify:
> 1. **Signal path:** peer-to-peer or through the master, and which path is used on each comms medium.
> 2. **Logic location:** which PLC decides start and stop. Recommended: the BPS PLC, using level data received from the reservoir.
> 3. **Data validity:** how staleness and bad quality are detected, with timeouts.
> 4. **Fallback behavior:** what happens on loss of valid level data, agreed under Section 4.4.
> 5. **Recovery:** how and when normal control resumes.
> 6. **Independent protection:** a secondary high-level signal, such as an independent level switch, that does not share the primary transmitter's failure modes.
>
> See Appendix F for a complete worked example.

### 5.9 Reservoir Sites

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| RES-001 | Each reservoir shall have a continuous level transmitter and an independent high-high level switch. | M | I |
| RES-002 | Reservoir site intrusion (hatch, door) shall be monitored and alarmed. | M | T |
| RES-003 | [Water quality monitoring, e.g. chlorine residual, if in scope] | | |

### 5.10 Time Synchronization
Specify the time source (e.g. GPS-referenced NTP), synchronization of all servers and PLCs, and the maximum allowable drift `[default: ±1 s]`.

### 5.11 External Interfaces
List interfaces to CMMS, GIS, LIMS, billing, and regulatory reporting. For each, specify direction, data, frequency, and security zone.

---

## 6. Non-Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-001 | Central SCADA availability shall be at least `[default: 99.9 %]`, measured annually, excluding planned maintenance. | M | A |
| NFR-002 | The system shall support growth of `[default: 50 %]` in I/O and `[default: 4]` additional sites without hardware replacement. | M | A |
| NFR-003 | Command execution time from operator action to field confirmation shall not exceed `[default: 5 s]` on primary comms. | M | T |
| NFR-004 | All software shall be on vendor-supported versions with at least `[default: 5 years]` of remaining support at handover. | M | I |

---

## 7. Cybersecurity

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** Align these requirements with the utility's risk and resilience assessment and IT policy. Specify a zones-and-conduits architecture per IEC 62443. Assign a target security level per zone, with the utility's agreement. Don't relax requirements for vendor convenience. Remote access is a frequent attack path in water-sector incidents.

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| SEC-001 | The control network shall be segmented from the business network by a DMZ; no direct traffic shall pass between them. | M | I/T |
| SEC-002 | All user accounts shall be individual; shared accounts are prohibited except for documented break-glass accounts. | M | I |
| SEC-003 | Remote access shall require multi-factor authentication, be session-logged, and be enabled only on utility approval for a defined time window. | M | T |
| SEC-004 | All default passwords shall be changed before connection to any network. | M | I |
| SEC-005 | Unused ports and services shall be disabled on all devices. | M | I |
| SEC-006 | PLCs shall be configured to reject program changes unless [key switch in PROGRAM / authenticated session]. | M | T |
| SEC-007 | Security logs shall be forwarded to [UTILITY SIEM / log server]. | D | T |
| SEC-008 | The system shall support backup and tested restore of all configurations; restore shall be demonstrated at SAT. | M | T |

---

## 8. Migration and Cutover

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** Require a cutover plan, site by site, that keeps water supply continuous. Define the following:
> - Parallel operation of old and new systems, if any
> - Temporary manual operation, with staffing implications
> - Rollback criteria for each site
> - Restricted windows, such as no cutovers during peak demand months

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| MIG-001 | The integrator shall submit a cutover plan, approved by the utility before any site work. | M | I |
| MIG-002 | Each site cutover shall include a documented rollback procedure, executable within `[default: 4 h]`. | M | I |
| MIG-003 | Inter-site call relationships shall be tested end-to-end before the old system is decommissioned at either site. | M | T |

---

## 9. Testing and Acceptance

| Stage | Purpose | Location |
|---|---|---|
| FAT | Verify software and hardware against the FRS using simulated I/O | Integrator facility |
| SAT | Verify each site with real I/O and equipment | Each site |
| SIT | Verify end-to-end integration, including inter-site control and comms failover | System-wide |
| Operational acceptance | Trial period of `[default: 30 days]` with no critical defects | Live |

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** Every Mandatory requirement must map to at least one test in the traceability matrix. For inter-site functions, require tests of every failure mode: primary comms loss, both paths lost, transmitter failure, central server loss, and recovery from each.

---

## 10. Documentation and Training

**Deliverables:** functional design specification, control narratives, I/O list, alarm philosophy and alarm list, network drawings, cybersecurity plan, test procedures and records, O&M manuals, as-built drawings, source code and configuration backups.

**Training:** operator, technician, and administrator courses. Specify duration, class size, and materials, and require recordings if needed.

### Appendix F – Worked Example: BPS-03 Called from RES-02 Level

> **AUTHOR GUIDANCE:** This example shows the level of detail expected. The numbers are illustrative only. Derive actual values from reservoir geometry, overflow elevation, pump capacity, demand data, and the operator response time agreed in Section 4.4.

**Context:** BPS-03 has two fixed-speed pumps (duty/standby, with lag on high demand) and fills RES-02, an elevated reservoir 4 km away. RES-02 has a level transmitter (LT-201) and an independent high-high float switch (LSHH-201). The overflow is at 95 % of operating range.

**Design decision (recorded):** Control logic resides in the BPS-03 PLC. RES-02 level is sent peer-to-peer from the RES-02 PLC to the BPS-03 PLC over licensed radio, and over cellular via the central SCADA as backup. This means a central server outage doesn't affect control while radio is healthy.

#### F.1 Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Rationale | Pri. | Ver. | Acceptance Criteria |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BPS03-010 | In Remote Auto, the BPS-03 PLC shall start the duty pump when RES-02 level (LT-201) falls to or below the lead start level `[60 %]`, and stop it when level rises to or above the lead stop level `[85 %]`. | Maintains reservoir level within the operating band; the 25 % gap prevents short-cycling. | M | T | With simulated LT-201 ramped down to 60 %, the duty pump starts within 1 scan + comms update (≤ 20 s). Ramped up to 85 %, it stops within the same time. |
| BPS03-011 | The PLC shall start the lag pump when level falls to or below `[45 %]` with the duty pump running, and stop the lag pump at `[75 %]`. | Meets peak demand. | M | T | Lag pump starts and stops at stated levels. |
| BPS03-012 | Start and stop levels shall be adjustable by Supervisor-level users within engineer-set limits: start `[40–70 %]`, stop `[70–90 %]`, with stop level ≥ start level + `[10 %]`. | Operational flexibility while preventing overflow and short-cycling settings. | M | T | Out-of-range and inverted entries are rejected with a message. |
| BPS03-013 | Each pump shall have a minimum run time of `[10 min]` and a minimum off time of `[15 min]`, except that stop commands from protective interlocks, and the high-high stop in BPS03-018, shall override the minimum run time. | Motor start limits; protection must not be delayed. | M | T | A level-based stop before 10 min is deferred; LSHH-201 stops the pump immediately. |
| BPS03-014 | The BPS-03 PLC shall treat RES-02 level as **invalid** when any of these occur: (a) no update received within `[60 s]` on any path; (b) RES-02 PLC reports LT-201 bad quality; (c) the level rate-of-change exceeds `[5 %/min]` sustained for `[30 s]`. | Detects comms loss, instrument failure, and implausible values before they drive control. | M | T | Each condition, injected separately, sets the invalid flag within the stated time, and the system raises the alarm "BPS-03: RES-02 LEVEL INVALID". |
| BPS03-015 | On loss of the radio path, the BPS-03 PLC shall continue control using level data received via the cellular backup without any change in pump state. | Comms redundancy must be transparent to the process. | M | T | With radio disabled, pump control continues per BPS03-010 with no spurious start or stop. Comms alarm raised. |
| BPS03-016 | When RES-02 level becomes invalid, the BPS-03 PLC shall maintain the current pump state for `[15 min]` and then enter the **fallback mode** selected by the engineer from: (a) stop all pumps; (b) time-based cycling `[run X min / off Y min]`; (c) control on BPS-03 discharge pressure `[start ≤ P1, stop ≥ P2]`. Default: `[(b) — to be confirmed by utility, see Sec. 4.4]`. | Short hold rides through brief outages; fallback balances overflow risk against supply loss per the utility's degraded operation priorities. | M | T | Each fallback option is tested: after 15 min invalid, the system behaves as selected and raises the alarm "BPS-03 IN FALLBACK MODE" as critical with callout. |
| BPS03-017 | The `[15 min]` hold time shall not exceed the time for RES-02 to rise from the lead stop level to overflow at the maximum BPS-03 flow and minimum demand, less a `[50 %]` safety margin. The integrator shall submit this calculation. | Ensures that a pump running at the moment of data loss cannot overflow the reservoir during the hold. | M | A | Calculation reviewed and accepted by the engineer. |
| BPS03-018 | Activation of LSHH-201 shall be transmitted to BPS-03 as a separate signal and shall stop all BPS-03 pumps in all modes except Local Hand, regardless of LT-201 value or validity, and shall latch until reset by an operator. | Independent protection against transmitter failure that reads low; prevents overflow. | M | T | With LT-201 forced to 50 %, actuating LSHH-201 stops pumps. They don't restart until reset. |
| BPS03-019 | If comms are lost to the extent that LSHH-201 status cannot be received, the alarm "BPS-03: RES-02 HIGH-HIGH PROTECTION UNAVAILABLE" shall be raised as a critical alarm. | Operators must know when overflow protection is not available. | M | T | Alarm raised within `[60 s]` of total comms loss. |
| BPS03-020 | When valid RES-02 level is restored and has remained valid for `[2 min]`, the PLC shall automatically return to normal control per BPS03-010, while respecting minimum run and off times, and log the transition. | Avoids flapping on intermittent comms; restores automatic control without operator intervention. | M | T | After comms are restored, normal control resumes after 2 min with no immediate start/stop violation of BPS03-013. |
| BPS03-021 | Loss of both central SCADA servers shall not affect BPS-03 control while the radio path between RES-02 and BPS-03 is healthy. | The central system supervises; it is not in the control path. | M | T | With both servers shut down, BPS-03 continues to respond to RES-02 level changes. |
| BPS03-022 | The HMI shall display, for BPS-03: RES-02 level with data quality, active comms path, time since last valid update, current control mode (Normal / Hold / Fallback), and remaining hold time. | Operators need the basis of the current control decision. | M | D | All items visible on the BPS-03 Level 2 display and updated live. |

#### F.2 Test Scenarios for SIT (Minimum)

| # | Scenario | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Normal fill/draw cycle | Starts/stops at configured levels |
| 2 | Radio path failure | Seamless transfer to cellular, comms alarm |
| 3 | Radio and cellular both fail, pump running | Hold 15 min, then fallback mode, critical alarm + callout |
| 4 | Radio and cellular both fail, pump stopped | Hold 15 min, then fallback mode |
| 5 | LT-201 fails low (3.5 mA) | Invalid → hold → fallback; LSHH-201 remains effective |
| 6 | LT-201 frozen at a valid value | Detected by [stale-value / rate checks, if specified]; see the note below |
| 7 | LSHH-201 activates with LT-201 reading normal | Immediate stop, latched |
| 8 | Both central servers offline | Local control unaffected |
| 9 | Comms restored after fallback | Return to normal after 2 min stable |
